limitations: Screening result on unvalidated, uncalibrated models; no plant validation is claimed.
The score is an ordinal evidence tally (supports 3/2/1 minus contradictions 6/2/1 for strong/moderate/weak), not a probability and not a certified cause.
The chatter model is linear: it cannot predict limit-cycle amplitude, mark severity or strip break, and a forced response at an unstable operating point is formal only.
Strip spans are lumped springs (inaccurate near the span wave resonance c/(2L)).
Circular (Hitchcock) roll flattening is not valid toward foil gauges; thinner passes need supplied bite sensitivities (model_options.bite_response_override).
The bite-damping closure (fraction beta of transit time) is a declared heuristic; results without it (beta = 0) are reported alongside.
Friction is an input unless tribology.use_computed_friction is set; the friction-speed closure of bite_tribology is an unfitted placeholder whose slope, not level, is used.
Fifth-octave regeneration (backup-roll marking) is screened kinematically, not simulated in time; the antisymmetric mode frequency is an undamped lumped estimate.
Spray coverage is a geometric footprint count; the phase-1 thermal growth is a free-expansion upper bound with no axial conduction (the v2 width_model solves the roll temperature field instead).
The lengthwise physics (roll thermal stripes, shape chain, coil ridges, troughs) rests on planner-derived and memory formulas flagged in each result; no plant validation.
The plane-strain factor is the isotropic 2/sqrt(3); published r-values of one 16 um 1235-H18 foil would move it by -12 % to +1 % under Hill's 1948 criterion (table in docs/thin-gauge-products.md).

flow_stress.note: Equivalent strain eps = prior + (2/sqrt(3))*ln(h_ref/h); the mean flow stress of each pass is the strain average over that pass (bite_tribology.schedule_flow_stress).

friction.note: PLACEHOLDER friction closure (not fitted): its end values 0.09 and 0.008 match the one abstract on aluminium [BT-S6 AB], but it keeps friction near 0.09 over most of the common industrial film-ratio window (0.01-0.5), so neither its level nor its slope with speed (dmu/du) is supported. With use_computed_friction the friction is a fixed point friction -> bite -> R' -> friction (at most 5 passes, tolerance 0.0001); otherwise it is evaluated once at the contact radius of the supplied-friction bite.

Same single-stand four-high aluminium mill as thin_gauge_chatter_demo, final pass 0.30 -> 0.21 mm at 12 m/s, friction 0.03 supplied (the placeholder tribology closure is shown beside it, not used), flow stress computed from a synthetic Voce law (use_computed_flow_stress true), schedule 2.2 -> 0.21 mm in six passes. Work-roll spray header: 32 nozzles at 52 mm pitch, 0.2 m standoff, 0.8 rad fans, mean spray coefficient 3 kW/m2K; nozzle 12 PARTLY blocked (flow level 0.45, continuous band of 2.72 um, chosen so that it stays latent in the mill on the thicker passes and buckles in the mill only at final gauge); zone switching: nozzles 20-21 off for 60 s and nozzle 6 off for 150 s (short-lived bands). The roll heat share (0.08 per roll, strip_heat_fraction 0.84) and the spray coefficient were CHOSEN so that the thermal crown lands in the 2-16 um reported for mills (model: 9.2 um). Observations were GENERATED FROM THE MODEL ITSELF (cells 256, default thermal numerics): band positions = model steady stripe peak and the two event stripe peaks rounded to 1 mm (0.357, 0.667, 1.093 m), intermittent duration = mean model visible time of the event bands (time above the in-mill manifest threshold) rounded to 10 s (40 s), continuity both, loose/buckle appearance and visible in the mill (the model bands are MANIFEST in the mill at the final pass), positions repeat across coils and do not move after a work-roll change, worse at thinner gauge. The case therefore tests the screening logic, not the physics.

Log the coolant valve states against the shapemeter zones and the band appearance times; compare the band duration with the valve-off intervals.
Vary the span tension and watch the bands; check roll alignment and crown of the deflector / idler rolls; measure the trough spacing.
Record whether the marks appear on both strip faces or only one.
Entry profile scan of the incoming coil and an outside-profile scan of the wound coil (ridges; worse toward the outer wraps?).

gauge_trend.own_stripe_text: The text above holds the case-pass stripe on every pass. The stripe each pass would itself produce scales with that pass's bite heat (same spray, same nozzle, steady state; the roll needs minutes to reach it, radial time constant about 4-7 min computed for a 260 mm roll [PT-T25]): at the case heat share it would buckle in the mill on P2, P3, P4, P5, P6; it would stay latent on P1. gauge_trend.reference_stripe_basis: largest steady stripe (peak 2.715e-06 m at 0.6675 m), isolated; onsets by scaling its own shape
gauge_trend.reference_stripe_description: smooth Gaussian stripe, half-peak width 0.1 m (about one cooling zone), centred at 0.6705 m; its height is bisected for the *_onset_height_reference_m columns
gauge_trend.text: Same 2.71 um roll stripe on every pass, 1.4 mm -> 0.21 mm: linear-feedback I-units 33.2 -> 50.7 (x1.53; rigid bound x6.67). In the mill this stripe buckles on 1 of 6 passes (utilisation 0.12 -> 1.4e+03); after tension release on 6 of 6 (utilisation 4.3 -> 2.4e+03). State changes along the schedule at P6 0.30->0.21 mm: MANIFEST_BUCKLE / MANIFEST_AFTER_TENSION_RELEASE. Onset stripe height, model stripe: in the mill 3.61 um -> 2.44 um, after release 0.626 um -> 0.108 um (reporting-threshold limited). Onset stripe height, Gaussian reference: in the mill 4.65 um -> 2.33 um, after release 2.07 um -> 0.0964 um (reporting-threshold limited). For the model stripe the gauge trend is carried by the after-release onset (thick/thin ratio 5.8 against 1.5). For the Gaussian reference the gauge trend is carried by the after-release onset (thick/thin ratio 21 against 2). After-release onsets on P3 0.90->0.60 mm, P4 0.60->0.42 mm, P5 0.42->0.30 mm, P6 0.30->0.21 mm are limited by the 2 I-unit reporting threshold (a band must first be reported), so they are upper bounds of the buckling onset. Flatness dead band half-width 13.9 -> 0.407 I-units.

thermal_events.attribution_definition: event metrics use the monitor history from the event start to attribution_window_end_s: the start of the next event switching nozzles within the isolation margin (0.1 m) of this one, else the end of the run; a fade beyond it gives only a lower bound (flag FADE_BEYOND_ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW), a later event starting during this one truncates its peak (flag PEAK_TRUNCATED_BY_LATER_EVENT); an earlier event in the same neighbourhood leaves its residual in the history (flag EARLIER_EVENT_IN_SAME_REGION)
thermal_events.band_life_definition: band_life_s = event duration + time after the event ends for the stripe to fall below the manifest threshold (or the reporting threshold when it never becomes manifest)
thermal_events.growth_rate_note: Radius growth follows the radial heat integral, so right after a spray change the stripe grows at 2*alpha*factor*dq/(rho*c) whatever the radial distribution; short-lived bands arise because the stripe crosses the manifest threshold within seconds to tens of seconds and fades over about a minute after the zone returns, not because the roll skin responds fast.
thermal_events.open_discrepancy: The 20 s first-order flatness response identified on a plant (Dohmae & Okamura 2012) is faster than this model's decay; possible causes (none modelled): bite heat depending on the roll surface temperature, emulsion-level heat transfer, per-revolution effects.
thermal_events.stripe_definition: one monitor per connected group of adjacent switched nozzles (a stripe); the stripe with the largest peak radius deviation governs the event metrics (governing_stripe_index), the others are listed under stripes
thermal_events.visible_time_definition: visible_time_s = time above the in-mill manifest threshold if reached, else above the after-release threshold, else above the reporting threshold (visible_time_basis says which); thresholds are stripe heights at the monitor position, from the peak profile scaled (onsets on a >= 10 mm grid), for the band at the stripe peak, where the peak states are read (bands elsewhere: neighbour_bands, never evidence)
